name: Sonnet contrarian turnarounds
strategy: Rotate into confirmed sector breakouts/breakdowns (financials, healthcare, biotech momentum, gold-miner and semi-extreme mean reversion) plus a defensive low-vol/utilities vs discretionary relative-value pair, rather than betting on beaten-down single names or fading crowded fear trades.

positions.thesis: Regional banks' credit-cycle tailwind remains intact (12mo total return +26.1%); holding size on a confirmed uptrend.
Healthcare's rotation is accelerating further (+7.3% in the past month vs the +4.0% noted at inception) — increasing on a confirmed breakout.
Still up sharply (YTD +23.6%, 1yr +72.7%) but showing a clear momentum pause (-6.6%/1mo) — trimming modestly while keeping a core position for H2 catalysts.
Defensive ballast is doing its job modestly (+3.7% YTD) but offers little torque — trimming to fund higher-conviction breakout/breakdown trades.
Utilities are pausing short-term (-1.5%/1mo) but still up YTD (+6.6%) on the AI-power-demand tailwind — holding as the long leg of the discretionary pair.

Miners' breakdown has largely played out (-15.3% YTD, -34.4%/6mo) and is now decelerating (-2.8%/1mo) as gold stabilizes (+0.7%/1mo) — trimming and lowering the take-profit to lock in the already-realized gain and cut squeeze risk.

The standout call in this book: the leveraged-semis mean-reversion short is a confirmed, still-accelerating crash (-42.9%/1mo, -61.1%/3mo) — sizing up materially while the trend is working, with stops to cap squeeze risk.
Discretionary remains the weakest S&P sector (YTD -6.8%) — holding as the short leg of the utilities relative-value pair.

reassessment_note: Unrestricted-retail resize (2026-07-30, free internet + no sizing caps): The semi-extreme mean-reversion short (SOXL) is the standout confirmed breakdown in this book too — down -42.9%/1mo and -61.1%/3mo, still accelerating — so I'm sizing it up materially from 8% to 20% with protective stops. GDX's breakdown, by contrast, is decelerating (-2.8%/1mo vs the sharp -13.2%/1mo noted at inception) as gold itself stabilizes (+0.7%/1mo), raising squeeze risk on further downside bets, so I'm trimming that short from 10% to 8% and lowering the take-profit to lock in the already-large realized gain (-15.3% YTD / -34.4% 6mo). XLV's breakout is confirming further (+7.3% in the past month) — increasing. XBI has cooled after a huge run (-6.6% 1mo despite +23.6% YTD) and USMV is low-torque ballast — both trimmed modestly to fund the SOXL add. KRE, XLU and XLY are holding up as thesised and are left roughly unchanged.
novelty: Only SOXL-short (20% in both books) repeats across Round 2 and Round 3; overlap = min(20,20)/95 ≈ 21% of Round 3's gross position weight, well under the 50% cap — Round 3 otherwise runs entirely on sector-ETF breakout/breakdown and relative-value pair trades (KRE/XLV/XBI/USMV/XLU/GDX/XLY) that are structurally distinct from Round 2's single-name-equity-and-crypto turnaround bets (ADBE/CRM/PYPL/BTC/ETH/IWM/GLD).
